title: Free dive
empty: No new field guide entries this dive.
radio: R-1, Control. Depth received. Mind the tether astern.

notes.bow: A raised forecastle helps keep seas off the forward deck.
notes.chain: Heavy interlocking links connect the anchor to the vessel.
notes.hatch: The raised coaming keeps deck water out of the cargo hold.
notes.bridge: Wide bridge windows give the watch a view over the sides.
notes.screw: Pitched blades push water astern as the shaft rotates.
notes.windlass: The windlass lifts the chain by engaging its links in a pocketed wheel.
notes.rail: A bent railing can catch the tether as it slides along the deck edge.
notes.silt: Fine sediment settles in the sheltered water of the hold.
notes.frames: Transverse frames stiffen the hull plating.
notes.poolwall: A straight pool wall provides a visual reference for station keeping.
notes.pile: Piles carry pier loads down into the seabed.
notes.leg: Braces connect jacket legs so the frame resists lateral loads.
notes.keel: A bilge keel damps rolling through water resistance.
notes.coral: The skeletons of reef-building corals shelter small fish.
notes.seastar: Sea stars move on tube feet under their arms.
notes.rope_coil: Loops of coiled rope can catch a passing tether.
notes.shackle: A removable pin closes the shackle around rigging.
notes.barnacle: Barnacles sweep food from the current with feathery limbs.
notes.grate_fish: Small fish can shelter between the bars of a grate.
notes.scuff: A scrape through the coating exposes the steel to seawater.
notes.feed: Uneaten feed can accumulate beneath a net pen.
notes.anemone_clump: Anemones capture prey with stinging cells on their tentacles.
notes.shell_bed: Waves and currents can move shell fragments into beds.
notes.rust_panel: Steel exposed by flaking paint corrodes in oxygenated seawater.
